tags: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre samavetāḥ yuyutsavaḥ māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kim akurvata sañjaya
dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca | dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ | māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata sañjaya ||1||
docs.text: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do when they assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager to fight?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.1

tags: sañjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍava-anīkam vyūḍham duryodhanaḥ ācāryam upasaṅgamya rājā vacanam abravīt
sañjaya uvāca | dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṁ vyūḍhaṁ duryodhanas tadā | ācāryam upasaṅgamya rājā vacanam abravīt ||2||
docs.text: Sanjaya said: Having seen the army of the Pandavas arrayed in battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher Drona and spoke these words.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.2

tags: paśya etām pāṇḍu-putrāṇām ācārya mahatīm camūm vyūḍhām drupada-putreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
paśyaitāṁ pāṇḍu-putrāṇām ācārya mahatīṁ camūm | vyūḍhāṁ drupada-putreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||3||
docs.text: Behold, O Teacher, this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged by your intelligent disciple, the son of Drupada.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.3

tags: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjuna-samā yudhi | yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahā-rathaḥ ||4||
atra śūrāḥ maheṣvāsāḥ bhīmārjuna-samāḥ yudhi yuyudhānaḥ virāṭaḥ drupadaḥ mahā-rathaḥ
docs.text: Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna — Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great warrior.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.4

tags: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśirājaś ca vīryavān | purujit kuntibhojaś ca śaibyaś ca nara-puṅgavaḥ ||5||
dhṛṣṭaketuḥ cekitānaḥ kāśirājaḥ vīryavān purujit kuntibhojaḥ śaibyaḥ nara-puṅgavaḥ
docs.text: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the valiant King of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya — all great warriors.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.5

tags: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān | saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahā-rathāḥ ||6||
yudhāmanyuḥ vikrāntaḥ uttamaujāḥ vīryavān saubhadraḥ draupadeyāḥ sarve mahā-rathāḥ
docs.text: The brave Yudhamanyu, the valiant Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu), and the sons of Draupadi — all great chariot warriors.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.6

tags: asmākam tu viśiṣṭāḥ ye nibodha dvijottama nāyakāḥ mama sainyasya saṁjñārtham bravīmi
asmākaṁ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama | nāyakā mama sainyasya saṁjñārthaṁ tān bravīmi te ||7||
docs.text: But know also, O best of Brahmanas, the distinguished leaders of our side. I name them for your information.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.7

tags: bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiñjayaḥ | aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattis tathaiva ca ||8||
bhavān bhīṣmaḥ karṇaḥ kṛpaḥ samitiñjayaḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaḥ saumadattiḥ
docs.text: Yourself (Drona), Bhishma, Karna, Kripa — always victorious in battle — Ashwatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.8

tags: anye bahavaḥ śūrāḥ mad-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ nānā-śastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśāradāḥ
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā mad-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ | nānā-śastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśāradāḥ ||9||
docs.text: And many other heroes, armed with various weapons, all skilled in battle, who are ready to give up their lives for my sake.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.9

tags: aparyāptam tat asmākam balam bhīṣma-abhirakṣitam paryāptam eteṣām bhīma-abhirakṣitam
aparyāptaṁ tad asmākaṁ balaṁ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam | paryāptaṁ tv idam eteṣāṁ balaṁ bhīmābhirakṣitam ||10||
docs.text: Our army, protected by Bhishma, is unlimited, while their army, protected by Bhima, is limited.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.10

tags: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathā-bhāgam avasthitāḥ | bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||11||
ayaneṣu sarveṣu yathā-bhāgam avasthitāḥ bhīṣmam eva abhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarve
docs.text: All of you, stationed at your respective positions at every strategic point, must protect Bhishma at all costs.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.11

tags: tasya sañjanayan harṣam kuru-vṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ siṁha-nādam vinadya uccaiḥ śaṅkham dadhmau pratāpavān
tasya sañjanayan harṣaṁ kuru-vṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ | siṁha-nādaṁ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṁ dadhmau pratāpavān ||12||
docs.text: Then Bhishma, the grand old patriarch of the Kuru dynasty, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, bringing joy to Duryodhana.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.12

tags: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānaka-gomukhāḥ | sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat ||13||
tataḥ śaṅkhāḥ bheryaḥ paṇava-ānaka-gomukhāḥ sahasā abhyahanyanta saḥ śabdaḥ tumulaḥ abhavat
docs.text: Then conches, drums, tabors, kettledrums, and horns suddenly sounded together, and the noise was tumultuous.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.13

tags: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau | mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||14||
tataḥ śvetaiḥ hayaiḥ yukte mahati syandane sthitau mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
docs.text: Then, seated in a magnificent chariot drawn by white horses, Krishna and Arjuna blew their divine conches.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.14

tags: pāñcajanyam hṛṣīkeśaḥ devadattam dhanañjayaḥ pauṇḍram mahā-śaṅkham bhīma-karmā vṛkodaraḥ
pāñcajanyaṁ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṁ dhanañjayaḥ | pauṇḍraṁ dadhmau mahā-śaṅkhaṁ bhīma-karmā vṛkodaraḥ ||15||
docs.text: Krishna blew his conch Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, the doer of terrible deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.15

tags: anantavijayam rājā kuntī-putraḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaḥ sughoṣa-maṇipuṣpakau
anantavijayaṁ rājā kuntī-putro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ | nakuḥlaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣa-maṇipuṣpakau ||16||
docs.text: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.16

tags: kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahā-rathaḥ | dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ ||17||
kāśyaḥ parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī mahā-rathaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ virāṭaḥ sātyakiḥ aparājitaḥ
docs.text: The King of Kashi, the supreme archer, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.17

tags: drupadaḥ draupadeyāḥ sarvaśaḥ pṛthivī-pate saubhadraḥ mahā-bāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak
drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivī-pate | saubhadraś ca mahā-bāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||18||
docs.text: Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the mighty-armed Abhimanyu — all blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.18

tags: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṁ hṛdayāni vyadārayat | nabhaś ca pṛthivīṁ caiva tumulo 'bhyanunādayan ||19||
saḥ ghoṣaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām hṛdayāni vyadārayat nabhaḥ pṛthivīm tumulaḥ abhyanunādayan
docs.text: That tumultuous sound, resounding through earth and sky, shattered the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.19

tags: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapi-dhvajaḥ pravṛtte śastra-sampāte dhanuḥ udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ hṛṣīkeśam vākyam
atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapi-dhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastra-sampāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ | hṛṣīkeśaṁ tadā vākyam idam āha mahī-pate ||20||
docs.text: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and the clash of weapons about to begin, Arjuna, whose flag bears the emblem of Hanuman, took up his bow and spoke these words to Krishna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.20

tags: arjuna uvāca senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye ratham sthāpaya me acyuta
arjuna uvāca | senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me 'cyuta ||21||
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Achyuta (infallible Krishna), place my chariot between the two armies.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.21

tags: yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṁ yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān | kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇa-samudyame ||22||
yāvat etān nirīkṣe aham yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān kaiḥ mayā yoddhavyam raṇa-samudyame
docs.text: Let me see those who have come here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded Duryodhana in this great battle.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.22

tags: yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṁ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-cikīrṣavaḥ ||23||
yotsyamānān avekṣe aham ye ete samāgatāḥ dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheḥ yuddhe priya-cikīrṣavaḥ
docs.text: Let me see those who have assembled here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.23

tags: sañjaya uvāca evam uktaḥ hṛṣīkeśaḥ guḍākeśena bhārata senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
sañjaya uvāca | evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata | senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam ||24||
docs.text: Sanjaya said: O Bharata (Dhritarashtra), having been thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna placed the finest chariot in the middle of both armies.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.24

tags: bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣām mahīkṣitām uvāca pārtha paśya etān samavetān kurūn iti
bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣāṁ ca mahīkṣitām | uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti ||25||
docs.text: In the presence of Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, Krishna said: O Partha, behold all the Kurus assembled here.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.25

tags: tatra apaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn pitāmahān ācāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīn
tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha pitāmahān | ācāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīṁs tathā ||26||
docs.text: There Arjuna saw standing — fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.26

tags: śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayoḥ ubhayoḥ api | tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān ||27|| kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt |
śvaśurān suhṛdaḥ senayoḥ ubhayoḥ samīkṣya kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn kṛpayā parayā āviṣṭaḥ viṣīdan
docs.text: Seeing fathers-in-law and well-wishers in both armies, Arjuna, overwhelmed with deep compassion, spoke in sorrow.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.27

tags: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṁ svajanaṁ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṁ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ ca pariśuṣyati ||28||
dṛṣṭvā imam svajanam kṛṣṇa yuyutsum samupasthitam sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukham pariśuṣyati
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed and eager to fight, my limbs fail and my mouth is drying up.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.28

tags: vepathuś ca śarīre me roma-harṣaś ca jāyate | gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate ||29||
vepathuḥ śarīre roma-harṣaḥ jāyate gāṇḍīvam sraṁsate hastāt tvak paridahyate
docs.text: My body trembles, my hair stands on end, the Gandiva bow slips from my hand, and my skin is burning all over.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.29

tags: na ca śaknomy avasthātuṁ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ | nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava ||30||
na śaknomi avasthātum bhramati iva me manaḥ nimittāni paśyāmi viparītāni keśava
docs.text: I cannot stand steady, my mind seems to whirl, and I see adverse omens, O Keshava.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.30

tags: na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave | na kāṅkṣe vijayaṁ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṁ sukhāni ca ||31||
na śreyaḥ anupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave kāṅkṣe vijayam rājyam sukhāni
docs.text: I do not see any good in killing my own people in battle. I desire neither victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.31

tags: kim naḥ rājyena govinda bhogaiḥ jīvitena vā yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitam
kiṁ no rājyena govinda kiṁ bhogair jīvitena vā | yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṁ no rājyaṁ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca ||32||
docs.text: Of what use is kingdom to us, O Govinda? Of what use are pleasures or even life itself? Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures — they stand here in battle.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.32

tags: ta ete 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁs tyaktvā dhanāni ca | ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāḥ tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ ||33||
te ete avasthitāḥ yuddhe prāṇān tyaktvā dhanāni ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāḥ pitāmahāḥ
docs.text: Teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers — they stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.33

tags: mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ sambandhinaḥ etān na hantum icchāmi ghnataḥ api madhusūdana
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ sambandhinaḥ tathā | etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhusūdana ||34||
docs.text: Maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives — I do not wish to kill them, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.34

tags: api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kim nu mahī-kṛte nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān kā prītiḥ janārdana
api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṁ nu mahī-kṛte | ihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana ||35||
docs.text: Even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, let alone this earth — what pleasure can we derive from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, O Janardana?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.35

tags: pāpam eva āśrayet asmān hatvā ātatāyinaḥ tasmāt na arhāḥ svajanam katham sukhinaḥ syāma
pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ | tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣṭrān sa-bāndhavān | svajanaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava ||36||
docs.text: Sin alone would accrue to us by killing these aggressors. Therefore, we should not kill our own relatives. How can we be happy by killing our own people, O Madhava?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.36

tags: yady api ete na paśyanti lobha-upahata-cetasaḥ kula-kṣaya-kṛtam doṣam mitra-drohe pātakam
yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahata-cetasaḥ | kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ mitra-drohe ca pātakam ||37||
docs.text: Even though these people, whose minds are overcome by greed, see no fault in destroying the family or sin in betraying friends,
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.37

tags: katham na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpāt nivartitum kula-kṣaya-kṛtam doṣam prapaśyadbhiḥ
kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum | kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ prapaśyadbhir janārdana ||38||
docs.text: Why should we, who can clearly see the evil in destroying the family, not know enough to turn away from this sin, O Janardana?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.38

tags: kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ dharme naṣṭe kulam kṛtsnam adharmaḥ abhibhavati
kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ | dharme naṣṭe kulaṁ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta ||39||
docs.text: With the destruction of the family, the eternal family traditions are destroyed; when dharma is lost, adharma overtakes the entire family.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.39

tags: adharma-abhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya varṇa-saṅkaraḥ jāyate
adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ | strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ ||40||
docs.text: When adharma prevails, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupted; when women are corrupted, O Varshneya, there arises an unwanted mixture of social orders.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.40

tags: saṅkaraḥ narakāya eva kula-ghnānām kulasya patanti pitaraḥ lupta piṇḍa-udaka-kriyāḥ
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kula-ghnānāṁ kulasya ca | patanti pitaro hy eṣāṁ lupta-piṇḍodaka-kriyāḥ ||41||
docs.text: Such social confusion leads to hell for the family and its destroyers. The ancestors fall, deprived of their offerings of food and water.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.41

tags: doṣair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṁ varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ | utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ ||42||
doṣaiḥ etaiḥ kula-ghnānām varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāḥ śāśvatāḥ
docs.text: By the evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, causing social confusion, the eternal community and family traditions are destroyed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.42

tags: utsanna-kula-dharmāṇām manuṣyāṇām janārdana narake niyatam vāsaḥ bhavati iti anuśuśruma
utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ janārdana | narake niyataṁ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma ||43||
docs.text: O Janardana, we have heard that those whose family traditions are destroyed dwell in hell for an indefinite period.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.43

tags: aho bata mahat pāpam kartum vyavasitāḥ vayam rājya-sukha-lobhena hantum svajanam udyatāḥ
aho bata mahat pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam | yad rājya-sukha-lobhena hantuṁ svajanam udyatāḥ ||44||
docs.text: Alas! What a great sin we have decided to commit — driven by the greed for royal pleasures, we are prepared to kill our own people.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.44

tags: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastram śastra-pāṇayaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ raṇe hanyuḥ tat me kṣemataram bhavet
yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṁ śastra-pāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṁ bhavet ||45||
docs.text: It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, were to kill me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.45

tags: sañjaya uvāca evam uktvā arjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopasthe upāviśat visṛjya sa-śaram cāpam śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ
sañjaya uvāca | evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya sa-śaraṁ cāpaṁ śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ ||46||
docs.text: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 1.46

tags: sañjaya uvāca | taṁ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇākulekṣaṇam | viṣīdantam idaṁ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ ||1||
sañjayaḥ uvāca tam tathā kṛpayā āviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇa ākulekṣaṇam viṣīdantam idam vākyam madhusūdanaḥ
docs.text: Sanjaya said: To him who was thus overcome with compassion, whose eyes were filled with tears and agitated, and who was despondent, Madhusudana spoke these words.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.1

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca kutaḥ tvā kaśmalam idam viṣame samupasthitam anārya-juṣṭam asvargyam akīrti-karam arjuna
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṁ viṣame samupasthitam | anārya-juṣṭam asvargyam akīrti-karam arjuna ||2||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: From where has this weakness come upon you at this critical moment? It is not befitting a noble person, it does not lead to heaven, and it causes disgrace, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.2

tags: klaibyam mā sma gamaḥ pārtha na etat tvayi upapadyate kṣudram hṛdaya-daurbalyam tyaktvā uttiṣṭha parantapa
klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate | kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa ||3||
docs.text: Do not yield to this weakness, O Partha. It does not befit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and arise, O scorcher of foes!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.3

tags: arjuna uvāca | kathaṁ bhīṣmam ahaṁ saṅkhye droṇaṁ ca madhusūdana | iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv ari-sūdana ||4||
arjunaḥ uvāca katham bhīṣmam aham saṅkhye droṇam madhusūdana iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhau ari-sūdana
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, how can I fight with arrows in battle against Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of my worship, O destroyer of enemies?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.4

tags: gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyaḥ bhoktum bhaikṣyam loke hatvā artha-kāmān bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān
gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyo bhoktuṁ bhaikṣyam apīha loke | hatvārtha-kāmāṁs tu gurūn ihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān ||5||
docs.text: It would be better to live in this world by begging than to slay these noble teachers. If I kill them, all my enjoyments of wealth and desires will be stained with blood.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.5

tags: na ca etat vidmaḥ katarat naḥ garīyaḥ jayema jayeyuḥ yān hatvā na jijīviṣāmaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ | yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ ||6||
docs.text: We do not even know which is better for us — whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us. The sons of Dhritarashtra, after killing whom we would not wish to live, are standing before us.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.6

tags: kārpaṇya-doṣa upahata svabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvām dharma-sammūḍha-cetāḥ śreyaḥ niścitam brūhi śiṣyaḥ te aham śādhi mām prapannam
kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṁ dharma-sammūḍha-cetāḥ | yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṁ brūhi tan me śiṣyas te 'haṁ śādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam ||7||
docs.text: My nature is afflicted by the weakness of pity. My mind is confused about duty. I ask You — tell me decisively what is best for me. I am Your disciple. Instruct me, for I have surrendered unto You.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.7

tags: na hi prapaśyāmi mama apanudyāt śokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām avāpya bhūmau asapatnam ṛddham rājyam surāṇām ādhipatyam
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām | avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṁ rājyaṁ surāṇām api cādhipatyam ||8||
docs.text: I do not see what could remove this grief that is drying up my senses, even if I were to obtain a prosperous and unrivaled kingdom on earth or even sovereignty over the gods.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.8

tags: sañjaya uvāca | evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṁ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ | na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṁ babhūva ha ||9||
sañjayaḥ uvāca evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśam guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ na yotsye iti govindam tūṣṇīm babhūva
docs.text: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha (Krishna), Gudakesha (Arjuna), the scorcher of foes, said 'I shall not fight' and became silent.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.9

tags: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasan iva bhārata senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye viṣīdantam idam vacaḥ
tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata | senayorubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṁ vacaḥ ||10||
docs.text: O descendant of Bharata, Hrishikesha (Krishna), as if smiling, spoke these words to the grief-stricken Arjuna in the midst of the two armies.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.10

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca aśocyān anvaśocaḥ tvam prajñā-vādān bhāṣase gatāsūn agatāsūn na anuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṁ prajñā-vādāṁś ca bhāṣase | gatāsūn agatāsūṁś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||11||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.11

tags: na tu eva aham jātu na āsam tvam ime janādhipāḥ na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param
na tv evāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ | na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param ||12||
docs.text: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.12

tags: dehinaḥ asmin yathā dehe kaumāram yauvanam jarā tathā dehāntara-prāptiḥ dhīraḥ tatra na muhyati
dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā | tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati ||13||
docs.text: Just as the embodied soul continuously passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so does it pass into another body. The wise person is not deluded by this.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.13

tags: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ | āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata ||14||
mātrā-sparśāḥ tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ āgamāpāyinaḥ anityāḥ tān titikṣasva bhārata
docs.text: The contacts of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and are impermanent. Endure them, O Bharata.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.14

tags: yam hi na vyathayanti ete puruṣam puruṣarṣabha sama-duḥkha-sukham dhīram saḥ amṛtatvāya kalpate
yaṁ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha | sama-duḥkha-sukhaṁ dhīraṁ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate ||15||
docs.text: O best among men, the wise person to whom pleasure and pain are the same, whom these do not disturb — that person is fit for immortality.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.15

tags: na asataḥ vidyate bhāvaḥ abhāvaḥ sataḥ ubhayoḥ dṛṣṭaḥ antaḥ anayoḥ tattva-darśibhiḥ
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ | ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ ||16||
docs.text: The unreal has no existence, and the real never ceases to be. The truth about both has been seen by the seers of reality.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.16

tags: avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam | vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaścit kartum arhati ||17||
avināśi tu tat viddhi yena sarvam idam tatam vināśam avyayasya asya na kaścit kartum arhati
docs.text: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. No one can cause the destruction of this imperishable being.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.17

tags: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ | anāśino 'prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata ||18||
antavantaḥ ime dehāḥ nityasya uktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ anāśinaḥ aprameyasya tasmāt yudhyasva bhārata
docs.text: These bodies of the eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable embodied soul are said to have an end. Therefore, fight, O Bharata!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.18

tags: ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaś cainaṁ manyate hatam | ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate ||19||
yaḥ enam vetti hantāram manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ ayam na hanti na hanyate
docs.text: He who thinks this (soul) is the killer and he who thinks it is killed — both do not know. The soul neither kills nor is killed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.19

tags: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṁ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||20||
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācit ayam bhūtvā bhavitā na bhūyaḥ ajaḥ nityaḥ śāśvataḥ purāṇaḥ na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
docs.text: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die; nor having once existed does it cease to be. It is unborn, eternal, permanent, and primeval. It is not killed when the body is killed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.20

tags: veda avināśinam nityam enam ajam avyayam katham saḥ puruṣaḥ pārtha kam ghātayati hanti
vedāvināśinaṁ nityaṁ ya enam ajam avyayam | kathaṁ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam ||21||
docs.text: O Partha, how can a person who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and imperishable — whom does he kill, and whom does he cause to be killed?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.21

tags: vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naraḥ aparāṇi tathā śarīrāṇi jīrṇāni anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī
vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi | tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī ||22||
docs.text: As a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.22

tags: na enam chindanti śastrāṇi dahati pāvakaḥ kledayanti āpaḥ śoṣayati mārutaḥ
nainaṁ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ | na cainaṁ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||23||
docs.text: Weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.23

tags: acchedyaḥ ayam adāhyaḥ akledyaḥ aśoṣyaḥ nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇuḥ acalaḥ sanātanaḥ
acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca | nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṁ sanātanaḥ ||24||
docs.text: This soul cannot be cut, cannot be burned, cannot be wetted, and cannot be dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unchanging, immovable, and everlasting.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.24

tags: avyaktaḥ ayam acintyaḥ avikāryaḥ ucyate tasmāt evam viditvā enam na anuśocitum arhasi
avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate | tasmād evaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśocitum arhasi ||25||
docs.text: This soul is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing this, you should not grieve.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.25

tags: atha ca enam nitya-jātam nityam manyase mṛtam tathāpi mahā-bāho na śocitum arhasi
atha cainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛtam | tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho naivaṁ śocitum arhasi ||26||
docs.text: Even if you think the soul is perpetually born and perpetually dies, even then, O mighty-armed one, you should not grieve.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.26

tags: jātasya hi dhruvaḥ mṛtyuḥ dhruvam janma mṛtasya tasmāt aparihārye arthe na śocitum arhasi
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṁ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṁ śocitum arhasi ||27||
docs.text: For one who is born, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over what is unavoidable.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.27

tags: avyakta-ādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata avyakta-nidhanāni eva tatra kā paridevanā
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata | avyakta-nidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā ||28||
docs.text: All beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest between birth and death, and unmanifest again after death. So what is there to grieve about, O Bharata?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.28

tags: āścarya-vat paśyati kaścid enam āścarya-vad vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ | āścarya-vac cainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpy enaṁ veda na caiva kaścit ||29||
āścarya-vat paśyati kaścit enam vadati tathā anyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvā api veda na
docs.text: Some look upon the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, some hear of it as a wonder, and even after hearing about it, no one truly knows it.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.29

tags: dehī nityam avadhyaḥ ayam dehe sarvasya bhārata tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na śocitum arhasi
dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata | tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śocitum arhasi ||30||
docs.text: The soul dwelling in the body of every being is eternally indestructible, O Bharata. Therefore, you should not grieve for any living being.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.30

tags: sva-dharmam api avekṣya na vikampitum arhasi dharmyāt hi yuddhāt śreyaḥ anyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
sva-dharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi | dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate ||31||
docs.text: Considering your own duty also, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is nothing better than a righteous battle.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.31

tags: yadṛcchayā copapannaṁ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam | sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam ||32||
yadṛcchayā upapannam svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam
docs.text: Happy are the warriors, O Partha, who obtain such an unsought opportunity for battle, which is an open gate to heaven.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.32

tags: atha cet tvam imam dharmyam saṅgrāmam na kariṣyasi sva-dharmam kīrtim hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
atha cet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣyasi | tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi ||33||
docs.text: But if you do not fight this righteous battle, then having abandoned your duty and honor, you will incur sin.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.33

tags: akīrtim bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te avyayām sambhāvitasya akīrtiḥ maraṇāt atiricyate
akīrtiṁ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām | sambhāvitasya cākīrtir maraṇād atiricyate ||34||
docs.text: People will speak of your everlasting dishonor, and for a respected person, dishonor is worse than death.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.34

tags: bhayād raṇād uparataṁ maṁsyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ | yeṣāṁ ca tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam ||35||
bhayāt raṇāt uparatam maṁsyante tvām mahā-rathāḥ bahu-mataḥ bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
docs.text: The great warriors will think you retreated from battle out of fear, and you who were once held in high esteem will fall into insignificance.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.35

tags: avācya-vādān bahūn vadiṣyanti tava ahitāḥ nindantaḥ sāmarthyam tataḥ duḥkhataram nu kim
avācya-vādāṁś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ | nindantas tava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim ||36||
docs.text: Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, slandering your ability. What could be more painful than that?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.36

tags: hataḥ vā prāpsyasi svargam jitvā bhokṣyase mahīm tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm | tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ ||37||
docs.text: If slain, you will attain heaven; if victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.37

tags: sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau tataḥ yuddhāya yujyasva na pāpam avāpsyasi
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi ||38||
docs.text: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, engage in battle. Thus you shall not incur sin.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.38

tags: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṁ śṛṇu | buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi ||39||
eṣā te abhihitā sāṅkhye buddhiḥ yoge imām śṛṇu buddhyā yuktaḥ karma-bandham prahāsyasi
docs.text: This wisdom has been declared to you according to Sankhya (analytical knowledge). Now hear it according to Yoga (the path of action). Endowed with this wisdom, O Partha, you shall be freed from the bondage of action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.39

tags: na iha abhikrama-nāśaḥ asti pratyavāyaḥ na vidyate svalpam api asya dharmasya trāyate mahataḥ bhayāt
nehābhikrama-nāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate | svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||40||
docs.text: In this path, no effort is ever lost, and there is no adverse result. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.40

tags: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana | bahu-śākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām ||41||
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ ekā iha kuru-nandana bahu-śākhāḥ hi anantāḥ buddhayaḥ avyavasāyinām
docs.text: O joy of the Kurus, the resolute intelligence of a person on this path is single-pointed. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.41

tags: yām imām puṣpitām vācam pravadanti avipaścitaḥ veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha na anyat asti vādinaḥ
yām imāṁ puṣpitāṁ vācaṁ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ | veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ ||42||
docs.text: The unwise utter flowery speech, O Partha, being attached to the ritualistic portions of the Vedas, saying there is nothing else.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.42

tags: kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā janma-karma-phala-pradām | kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati ||43||
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parāḥ janma-karma-phala-pradām kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulām bhogaiśvarya-gatim prati
docs.text: Full of desires, with heaven as their highest goal, they prescribe various specific rituals aimed at enjoyment and power, leading to rebirth as the result of their actions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.43

tags: bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānām tayā apahṛta-cetasām vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛta-cetasām | vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||44||
docs.text: For those who are deeply attached to enjoyment and power, whose minds are carried away by such flowery words, the resolute determination for meditation does not arise.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.44

tags: trai-guṇya-viṣayā vedā nistrai-guṇyo bhavārjuna | nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān ||45||
trai-guṇya-viṣayāḥ vedāḥ nistrai-guṇyaḥ bhava arjuna nirdvandvaḥ nitya-sattva-sthaḥ niryoga-kṣemaḥ ātmavān
docs.text: The Vedas deal with the three modes of material nature. Rise above the three gunas, O Arjuna. Be free from dualities, ever established in purity, unconcerned with acquisition and preservation, and established in the Self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.45

tags: yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake | tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ ||46||
yāvān arthaḥ udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
docs.text: As much use as a well has when there is water flooding everywhere — that much use do all the Vedas have for an enlightened person who knows Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.46

tags: karmaṇi eva adhikāraḥ te mā phaleṣu kadācana karma-phala-hetuḥ bhūḥ saṅgaḥ astu akarmaṇi
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||47||
docs.text: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.47

tags: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgam tyaktvā dhanañjaya siddhyasiddhyoḥ samaḥ bhūtvā samatvam yogaḥ ucyate
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya | siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga ucyate ||48||
docs.text: Perform actions being established in yoga, abandoning attachment, O Dhananjaya. Be equal in success and failure; this equanimity is called yoga.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.48

tags: dūreṇa hi avaram karma buddhi-yogāt dhanañjaya buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
dūreṇa hy avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya | buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ ||49||
docs.text: Action performed with selfish motive is far inferior to the yoga of wisdom, O Dhananjaya. Seek refuge in wisdom; wretched are those whose motive is the fruit of action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.49

tags: buddhi-yuktaḥ jahāti iha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte tasmāt yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte | tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam ||50||
docs.text: Endowed with the wisdom of equanimity, one casts off in this life both good and evil deeds. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.50

tags: karma-jam buddhi-yuktāḥ hi phalam tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padam gacchanti anāmayam
karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ | janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gacchanty anāmayam ||51||
docs.text: The wise, endowed with evenness of mind, renouncing the fruits born of action, are freed from the bondage of birth and attain the state beyond all suffering.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.51

tags: yadā te moha-kalilam buddhiḥ vyatitariṣyati tadā gantāsi nirvedam śrotavyasya śrutasya
yadā te moha-kalilaṁ buddhir vyatitariṣyati | tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca ||52||
docs.text: When your intellect crosses beyond the mire of delusion, then you shall attain indifference to what has been heard and what is yet to be heard.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.52

tags: śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā samādhau acalā buddhiḥ tadā yogam avāpsyasi
śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā | samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi ||53||
docs.text: When your intellect, bewildered by the conflicting teachings of the scriptures, shall stand firm and steady in meditation, then you shall attain yoga.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.53

tags: arjuna uvāca | sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava | sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣeta kim āsīta vrajeta kim ||54||
arjunaḥ uvāca sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava sthita-dhīḥ kim prabhāṣeta āsīta vrajeta
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Keshava, what is the description of one of steady wisdom, who is absorbed in deep meditation? How does the one of steady wisdom speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.54

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān ātmani ātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñaḥ tadā ucyate
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān | ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadocyate ||55||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: When a man completely casts off all the desires of the mind, O Partha, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self alone, then he is said to be one of steady wisdom.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.55

tags: duḥkheṣu anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ vīta rāga bhaya krodhaḥ sthita-dhīḥ muniḥ ucyate
duḥkheṣv anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ | vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir ucyate ||56||
docs.text: He whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who does not long for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear, and anger — such a sage is called one of steady wisdom.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.56

tags: yaḥ sarvatra anabhisnehaḥ tat tat prāpya śubha aśubham na abhinandati dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham | nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||57||
docs.text: He who is without attachment everywhere, who neither rejoices nor hates on obtaining good or evil — his wisdom is firmly established.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.57

tags: yadā saṁharate ca ayam kūrmaḥ aṅgāni iva sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
yadā saṁharate cāyaṁ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||58||
docs.text: When he completely withdraws the senses from their objects, as a tortoise draws in its limbs from all sides, his wisdom is firmly established.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.58

tags: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ | rasa-varjaṁ raso 'py asya paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||59||
viṣayāḥ vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ rasa-varjam rasaḥ api asya param dṛṣṭvā nivartate
docs.text: The sense objects turn away from the embodied one who abstains from feeding them, but the taste for them remains. Even this taste ceases when the Supreme is realized.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.59

tags: yatataḥ hi api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabham manaḥ
yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ | indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ ||60||
docs.text: The turbulent senses, O son of Kunti, forcibly carry away the mind of even a wise person who is striving to control them.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.60

tags: tāni sarvāṇi saṁyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ | vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||61||
tāni sarvāṇi saṁyamya yuktaḥ āsīta mat-paraḥ vaśe hi yasya indriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
docs.text: Having restrained all the senses, one should sit steadfast, intent on Me; for his wisdom is steady whose senses are under control.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.61

tags: dhyāyataḥ viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgaḥ teṣu upajāyate saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodhaḥ abhijāyate
dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate | saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate ||62||
docs.text: When a person dwells on sense objects, attachment to them arises; from attachment springs desire; and from desire anger is born.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.62

tags: krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ | smṛti-bhraṁśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati ||63||
krodhāt bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ smṛti-bhraṁśāt buddhi-nāśaḥ buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati
docs.text: From anger arises delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, destruction of the intellect; and from destruction of the intellect, one perishes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.63

tags: rāga-dveṣa-viyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran | ātma-vaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati ||64||
rāga-dveṣa-viyuktaiḥ tu viṣayān indriyaiḥ caran ātma-vaśyaiḥ vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati
docs.text: But the self-controlled person, moving among sense objects with senses free from attraction and aversion and under the governance of the Self, attains serenity.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.64

tags: prasāde sarva-duḥkhānām hāniḥ asya upajāyate prasanna-cetasaḥ hi āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate | prasanna-cetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ||65||
docs.text: In that serenity, there arises the destruction of all sorrows; for the intellect of the serene-minded soon becomes firmly established.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.65

tags: na asti buddhiḥ ayuktasya bhāvanā abhāvayataḥ śāntiḥ aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
nāsti buddhir ayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā | na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ||66||
docs.text: There is no wisdom for the undisciplined, and no meditation for the undisciplined; for one who does not meditate there is no peace; and for the unpeaceful, how can there be happiness?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.66

tags: indriyāṇām hi caratām yat manaḥ anuvidhīyate tat asya harati prajñām vāyuḥ nāvam iva ambhasi
indriyāṇāṁ hi caratāṁ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate | tad asya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi ||67||
docs.text: For the mind that yields to the roaming senses carries away his wisdom, as the wind carries away a boat on the waters.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.67

tags: tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||68||
tasmāt yasya mahā-bāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
docs.text: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, his wisdom is firmly established whose senses are completely restrained from their objects on all sides.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.68

tags: yā niśā sarva-bhūtānām tasyām jāgarti saṁyamī yasyām jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyataḥ muneḥ
yā niśā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti saṁyamī | yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||69||
docs.text: That which is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; that in which all beings are awake is night for the sage who sees.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.69

tags: āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭham samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat tadvat kāmāḥ yam praviśanti sarve saḥ śāntim āpnoti kāma-kāmī
āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭhaṁ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat | tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī ||70||
docs.text: As the ocean remains unmoved though waters flow into it from all sides, so the one into whom all desires enter without disturbing attains peace — not the one who craves the fulfillment of desires.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.70

tags: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumān carati niḥspṛhaḥ nirmamaḥ nirahaṅkāraḥ saḥ śāntim adhigacchati
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṁś carati niḥspṛhaḥ | nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||71||
docs.text: That person who, having abandoned all desires, moves about free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego — he attains peace.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.71

tags: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha na enām prāpya vimuhyati sthitvā asyām anta-kāle api brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati | sthitvāsyām anta-kāle 'pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati ||72||
docs.text: This is the state of being established in Brahman, O Partha. Having attained this, one is never deluded. Being established in this state even at the hour of death, one attains liberation in Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 2.72

tags: arjuna uvāca jyāyasī cet karmaṇaḥ te matā buddhiḥ janārdana tat kim karmaṇi ghore mām niyojayasi keśava
arjuna uvāca | jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana | tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśava ||1||
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Janardana, O Keshava, if You consider knowledge to be superior to action, then why do You urge me to engage in this terrible action?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.1

tags: vyāmiśreṇa iva vākyena buddhim mohayasi iva me tat ekam vada niścitya yena śreyaḥ aham āpnuyām
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me | tad ekaṁ vada niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām ||2||
docs.text: With these seemingly contradictory words, You are confusing my intelligence. Tell me decisively the one path by which I may attain the highest good.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.2

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca loke asmin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayā anagha jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānām karma-yogena yoginām
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | loke 'smin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha | jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṁ karma-yogena yoginām ||3||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: O sinless one, in this world I have taught a twofold path from the beginning — the path of knowledge (Jnana Yoga) for the contemplative, and the path of action (Karma Yoga) for the active.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.3

tags: na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṁ puruṣo 'śnute | na ca sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigacchati ||4||
na karmaṇām anārambhāt naiṣkarmyam puruṣaḥ aśnute na ca sannyasanāt eva siddhim samadhigacchati
docs.text: Not by abstaining from action does a person attain freedom from action, nor by mere renunciation does one attain perfection.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.4

tags: na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhati akarmakṛt kāryate hi avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jaiḥ guṇaiḥ
na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt | kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ ||5||
docs.text: No one can remain even for a moment without performing action. Everyone is helplessly driven to act by the qualities born of material nature.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.5

tags: karma-indriyāṇi saṁyamya yaḥ āste manasā smaran indriya-arthān vimūḍha-ātmā mithyā-ācāraḥ saḥ ucyate
karmendriyāṇi saṁyamya ya āste manasā smaran | indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate ||6||
docs.text: One who restrains the organs of action but sits mentally dwelling on sense objects is deluded and is called a hypocrite.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.6

tags: yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate 'rjuna | karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate ||7||
yaḥ tu indriyāṇi manasā niyamya ārabhate arjuna karma-indriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ saḥ viśiṣyate
docs.text: But one who controls the senses with the mind and engages the organs of action in Karma Yoga without attachment — that person excels, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.7

tags: niyatam kuru karma tvam karma jyāyaḥ hi akarmaṇaḥ śarīra-yātrā api ca te na prasiddhyet akarmaṇaḥ
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ | śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ ||8||
docs.text: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible through inaction.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.8

tags: yajña-arthāt karmaṇaḥ anyatra lokaḥ ayam karma-bandhanaḥ tad-artham karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samācara
yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ | tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samācara ||9||
docs.text: Work done as a sacrifice for the Supreme alone does not bind. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your duty free from attachment, as an offering.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.9

tags: saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ | anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk ||10||
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purā uvāca prajāpatiḥ anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣaḥ vaḥ astu iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk
docs.text: In the beginning, the Creator, having created humankind together with sacrifice, said: By this shall you prosper; let this be the wish-fulfilling cow that grants all your desires.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.10

tags: devān bhāvayata anena te devāḥ bhāvayantu vaḥ parasparam bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ | parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha ||11||
docs.text: Nourish the gods through sacrifice, and the gods shall nourish you. Thus, nourishing one another, you shall attain the supreme good.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.11

tags: iṣṭān bhogān hi vaḥ devāḥ dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ taiḥ dattān apradāya ebhyaḥ yaḥ bhuṅkte stenaḥ eva saḥ
iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ | tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ ||12||
docs.text: The gods, nourished by sacrifice, will bestow upon you the enjoyments you desire. But one who enjoys their gifts without offering anything in return is indeed a thief.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.12

tags: yajña-śiṣṭa-aśinaḥ santaḥ mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ bhuñjate te tu agham pāpāḥ ye pacanti ātma-kāraṇāt
yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ | bhuñjate te tv aghaṁ pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt ||13||
docs.text: The righteous who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins. But the wicked who cook only for themselves — they eat nothing but sin.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.13

tags: annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ | yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ ||14||
annāt bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyāt anna-sambhavaḥ yajñāt bhavati parjanyaḥ yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ
docs.text: From food, beings are born. From rain, food is produced. From sacrifice, rain arises. And sacrifice is born of action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.14

tags: karma brahma-udbhavam viddhi brahma akṣara-samudbhavam tasmāt sarva-gatam brahma nityam yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣara-samudbhavam | tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||15||
docs.text: Know that action arises from the Vedas, and the Vedas arise from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading Brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.15

tags: evam pravartitam cakram na anuvartayati iha yaḥ aghāyuḥ indriyārāmaḥ mogham pārtha saḥ jīvati
evaṁ pravartitaṁ cakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ | aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati ||16||
docs.text: One who does not follow this wheel thus set in motion, who lives sinfully delighting only in the senses — that person lives in vain, O Partha.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.16

tags: yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś ca mānavaḥ | ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate ||17||
yaḥ tu ātma-ratiḥ eva syāt ātma-tṛptaḥ mānavaḥ ātmani eva santuṣṭaḥ tasya kāryam na vidyate
docs.text: But for one who delights in the Self alone, who is satisfied in the Self and content in the Self — for such a person, there is no duty to perform.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.17

tags: na eva tasya kṛtena arthaḥ na akṛtena iha kaścana na ca asya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścit artha-vyapāśrayaḥ
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana | na cāsya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ ||18||
docs.text: For such a person, there is no purpose to be gained by action done, nor anything lost by action not done. Nor does such a person depend on any being for any purpose.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.18

tags: tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācara | asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ ||19||
tasmāt asaktaḥ satatam kāryam karma samācara asaktaḥ hi ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ
docs.text: Therefore, always perform your obligatory duty without attachment. For by performing action without attachment, a person attains the Supreme.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.19

tags: karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ | loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśyan kartum arhasi ||20||
karmaṇā eva hi saṁsiddhim āsthitāḥ janaka-ādayaḥ loka-saṅgraham eva api sampaśyan kartum arhasi
docs.text: King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even considering the welfare of the world, you should act.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.20

tags: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ | sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate ||21||
yad yat ācarati śreṣṭhaḥ tat tat eva itaraḥ janaḥ saḥ yat pramāṇam kurute lokaḥ tat anuvartate
docs.text: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world follows.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.21

tags: na me pārtha asti kartavyam triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana na anavāptam avāptavyam varte eva ca karmaṇi
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana | nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva ca karmaṇi ||22||
docs.text: O Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I need to do, nor is there anything unattained that I need to attain — yet I continue to engage in action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.22

tags: yadi hi aham na varteyam jātu karmaṇi atandritaḥ mama vartma anuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
yadi hy ahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ | mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||23||
docs.text: For if I ever failed to engage in action without laziness, O Partha, people would follow My path in every way.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.23

tags: utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ced aham | saṅkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ ||24||
utsīdeyuḥ ime lokāḥ na kuryām karma cet aham saṅkarasya kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
docs.text: If I did not perform action, these worlds would perish. I would be the cause of confusion and would destroy these beings.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.24

tags: saktāḥ karmaṇi avidvāṁsaḥ yathā kurvanti bhārata kuryāt vidvān tathā asaktaḥ cikīrṣuḥ loka-saṅgraham
saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṁso yathā kurvanti bhārata | kuryād vidvāṁs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur loka-saṅgraham ||25||
docs.text: As the ignorant act with attachment to results, O Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.25

tags: na buddhi-bhedam janayet ajñānām karma-saṅginām joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām | joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran ||26||
docs.text: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Rather, performing all actions with devotion, the wise should inspire others to do the same.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.26

tags: prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ ahaṅkāra vimūḍhātmā kartā aham iti manyate
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ | ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate ||27||
docs.text: All actions are performed by the modes of material nature. But the soul deluded by ego thinks: 'I am the doer.'
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.27

tags: tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ guṇāḥ guṇeṣu vartante iti matvā na sajjate
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ | guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate ||28||
docs.text: But one who knows the truth about the divisions of the modes of nature and their actions, O mighty-armed one, understanding that it is the modes that act upon the modes, does not become attached.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.28

tags: prakṛter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu | tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsna-vin na vicālayet ||29||
prakṛteḥ guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu tān akṛtsna-vidaḥ mandān kṛtsna-vit na vicālayet
docs.text: Those deluded by the modes of nature become attached to the actions of the modes. The person of complete knowledge should not disturb those of incomplete understanding who are slow to learn.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.29

tags: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṁnyasya adhyātma-cetasā nirāśīḥ nirmamaḥ bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṁnyasyādhyātma-cetasā | nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ ||30||
docs.text: Surrendering all actions to Me, with a mind focused on the Self, free from desire and possessiveness, fight — free from anxiety.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.30

tags: ye me matam idam nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ śraddhāvantaḥ anasūyantaḥ mucyante te api karmabhiḥ
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ | śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ ||31||
docs.text: Those who constantly follow this teaching of Mine with faith and without envy are freed from the bondage of actions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.31

tags: ye tu etat abhyasūyantaḥ na anutiṣṭhanti me matam sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhān tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ
ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam | sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṁs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ ||32||
docs.text: But those who find fault with My teaching and do not follow it — know them to be deluded in all knowledge, devoid of sense, and ruined.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.32

tags: sadṛśam ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ jñānavān api prakṛtim yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kim kariṣyati
sadṛśaṁ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api | prakṛtiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣyati ||33||
docs.text: Even a wise person acts according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature. What can repression accomplish?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.33

tags: indriyasya indriyasya arthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau tayoḥ na vaśam āgacchet tau hi asya paripanthinau
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau | tayor na vaśam āgacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau ||34||
docs.text: Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses are seated in the senses. One should not come under the control of these two, for they are indeed one's enemies on the path.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.34

tags: śreyān sva-dharmaḥ viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt sva-dharme nidhanam śreyaḥ para-dharmaḥ bhayāvahaḥ
śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt | sva-dharme nidhanaṁ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||35||
docs.text: Better is one's own duty, though imperfectly performed, than the duty of another well performed. Better is death in the performance of one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with danger.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.35

tags: arjuna uvāca atha kena prayuktaḥ ayam pāpam carati pūruṣaḥ anicchann api vārṣṇeya balāt iva niyojitaḥ
arjuna uvāca | atha kena prayukto 'yaṁ pāpaṁ carati pūruṣaḥ | anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ ||36||
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Krishna, by what is a person impelled to commit sin, even unwillingly, as if compelled by force?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.36

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca kāmaḥ eṣaḥ krodhaḥ eṣaḥ rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ mahāśanaḥ mahā-pāpmā viddhi enam iha vairiṇam
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ | mahāśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam ||37||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the mode of passion, all-devouring and greatly sinful. Know this as the enemy here.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.37

tags: dhūmena āvriyate vahniḥ yathā ādarśaḥ malena yathā ulbena āvṛtaḥ garbhaḥ tathā tena idam āvṛtam
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena ca | yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam ||38||
docs.text: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, and as an embryo is covered by the womb, so is knowledge covered by desire.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.38

tags: āvṛtam jñānam etena jñāninaḥ nitya-vairiṇā kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇa analena
āvṛtaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā | kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca ||39||
docs.text: O son of Kunti, the knowledge of even the wise is covered by this eternal enemy in the form of desire, which is insatiable like fire.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.39

tags: indriyāṇi manaḥ buddhiḥ asya adhiṣṭhānam ucyate etaiḥ vimohayati eṣaḥ jñānam āvṛtya dehinam
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate | etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam ||40||
docs.text: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be the stronghold of desire. Through these, desire covers knowledge and deludes the embodied soul.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.40

tags: tasmāt tvam indriyāṇi ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha pāpmānam prajahi hi enam jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha | pāpmānaṁ prajahi hy enaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam ||41||
docs.text: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first controlling the senses, destroy this sinful destroyer of knowledge and realization.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.41

tags: indriyāṇi parāṇi āhuḥ indriyebhyaḥ param manaḥ manasaḥ tu parā buddhiḥ yaḥ buddheḥ parataḥ saḥ
indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ | manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ ||42||
docs.text: The senses are said to be superior to the body; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and that which is superior to the intellect is the Self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.42

tags: evam buddheḥ param buddhvā saṁstabhya ātmānam ātmanā jahi śatrum mahā-bāho kāma-rūpam durāsadam
evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā saṁstabhyātmānam ātmanā | jahi śatruṁ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṁ durāsadam ||43||
docs.text: Thus, knowing the Self to be superior to the intellect, and steadying the mind by the Self, O mighty-armed Arjuna, destroy this difficult-to-conquer enemy in the form of desire.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 3.43

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca imam vivasvate yogam proktavān aham avyayam vivasvān manave prāha manuḥ ikṣvākave abravīt
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam | vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣvākave 'bravīt ||1||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan (the sun-god); Vivasvan taught it to Manu (the father of mankind); and Manu taught it to Ikshvaku.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.1

tags: evam paramparā-prāptam imam rājarṣayaḥ viduḥ saḥ kālena iha mahatā yogaḥ naṣṭaḥ parantapa
evaṁ paramparā-prāptam imaṁ rājarṣayo viduḥ | sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa ||2||
docs.text: Thus received through the chain of disciplic succession, the saintly kings understood this yoga. But over a great passage of time, this yoga was lost in this world, O scorcher of foes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.2

tags: sa evāyaṁ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ | bhakto 'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṁ hy etad uttamam ||3||
saḥ eva ayam mayā te adya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ bhaktaḥ asi me sakhā ca iti rahasyam hi etat uttamam
docs.text: That very same ancient yoga has been today spoken by Me to you, because you are My devotee and My friend — for this is a supreme secret.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.3

tags: arjuna uvāca aparam bhavataḥ janma param janma vivasvataḥ katham etat vijānīyām tvam ādau proktavān iti
arjuna uvāca | aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ | katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti ||4||
docs.text: Arjuna said: Your birth is recent, and the birth of Vivasvan was in ancient times. How am I to understand that You taught this yoga in the beginning?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.4

tags: śrī-bhagavān uvāca bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava ca arjuna tāni aham veda sarvāṇi na tvam vettha parantapa
śrī-bhagavān uvāca | bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna | tāny ahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa ||5||
docs.text: The Blessed Lord said: Many births of Mine have passed, and many of yours too, O Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.5

tags: ajaḥ api san avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaraḥ api san prakṛtim svām adhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmi ātma-māyayā
ajo 'pi sann avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san | prakṛtiṁ svām adhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmy ātma-māyayā ||6||
docs.text: Though I am unborn, imperishable, and the Lord of all beings, I manifest Myself by controlling My own material nature through My divine power (maya).
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.6

tags: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata | abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham ||7||
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glāniḥ bhavati bhārata abhyutthānam adharmasya tadā ātmānam sṛjāmi aham
docs.text: Whenever there is a decline of dharma (righteousness) and a rise of adharma (unrighteousness), O Bharata, at that time I manifest Myself.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.7

tags: paritrāṇāya sādhūnām vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||8||
docs.text: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of dharma, I manifest Myself in every age.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.8

tags: janma karma ca me divyam evam yaḥ vetti tattvataḥ tyaktvā deham punar janma na eti mām eti saḥ arjuna
janma karma ca me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ | tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna ||9||
docs.text: One who truly knows the divine nature of My birth and actions, upon leaving the body, is not born again — but comes to Me, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.9

tags: vīta rāga bhaya krodhāḥ man-mayāḥ mām upāśritāḥ bahavaḥ jñāna-tapasā pūtāḥ mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśritāḥ | bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ ||10||
docs.text: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge — many have attained My state of being.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.10

tags: ye yathā mām prapadyante tān tathā eva bhajāmi aham mama vartma anuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham | mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||11||
docs.text: As they surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows My path in all respects, O son of Pritha.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.11

tags: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇām siddhim yajante iha devatāḥ kṣipram hi mānuṣe loke siddhiḥ bhavati karmajā
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ | kṣipraṁ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā ||12||
docs.text: Desiring success in their actions, people in this world worship the demigods. For in the human world, success born of action comes quickly.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.12

tags: cātur-varṇyam mayā sṛṣṭam guṇa karma vibhāgaśaḥ tasya kartāram api mām viddhi akartāram avyayam
cātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ | tasya kartāram api māṁ viddhy akartāram avyayam ||13||
docs.text: The four divisions of human society were created by Me according to differences in quality (guna) and action (karma). Though I am the creator of this system, know Me to be the imperishable non-doer.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.13

tags: na mām karmāṇi limpanti me karma-phale spṛhā iti yaḥ abhijānāti karmabhiḥ sa badhyate
na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā | iti māṁ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate ||14||
docs.text: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I desire the fruits of action. One who understands this truth about Me is never bound by actions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.14

tags: evam jñātvā kṛtam karma pūrvaiḥ api mumukṣubhiḥ kuru karma eva tasmāt tvam pūrvataram
evaṁ jñātvā kṛtaṁ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ | kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛtam ||15||
docs.text: Knowing this, the ancient seekers of liberation also performed action. Therefore, you too should perform action, as the ancients did in bygone times.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.15

tags: kim karma kim akarma iti kavayaḥ api atra mohitāḥ tat te pravakṣyāmi yat jñātvā mokṣyase aśubhāt
kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ | tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||16||
docs.text: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. I shall explain to you what action is, knowing which you shall be liberated from evil.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.16

tags: karmaṇaḥ hi api boddhavyam vikarmaṇaḥ akarmaṇaḥ gahanā karmaṇaḥ gatiḥ
karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṁ boddhavyaṁ ca vikarmaṇaḥ | akarmaṇaś ca boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ ||17||
docs.text: One must understand the nature of action, the nature of forbidden action, and the nature of inaction. The path of action is deep and difficult to understand.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.17

tags: karmaṇi akarma yaḥ paśyet akarmaṇi karma saḥ buddhimān manuṣyeṣu yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt
karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ | sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt ||18||
docs.text: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise among human beings. Such a person is a yogi and has accomplished all actions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.18

tags: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma saṅkalpa varjitāḥ jñānāgni dagdha karmāṇam tam āhuḥ paṇḍitam budhāḥ
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ | jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṁ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṁ budhāḥ ||19||
docs.text: One whose every undertaking is free from desire and selfish motive, and whose actions have been burned in the fire of knowledge — such a person is called wise by the knowledgeable.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.19

tags: tyaktvā karma-phala āsaṅgam nitya tṛptaḥ nirāśrayaḥ karmaṇi abhipravṛttaḥ api na eva kiñcit karoti saḥ
tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṁ nitya-tṛpto nirāśrayaḥ | karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi naiva kiñcit karoti saḥ ||20||
docs.text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content, depending on nothing — such a person, even though fully engaged in action, does nothing at all.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.20

tags: nirāśīr yata-cittātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ | śārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam ||21||
nirāśīḥ yata cittātmā tyakta sarva parigrahaḥ śārīram kevalam karma kurvan na āpnoti kilbiṣam
docs.text: One who is free from expectations, whose mind and self are fully controlled, who has abandoned all sense of ownership, and who performs actions only for the bare maintenance of the body — such a person incurs no sin.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.21

tags: yadṛcchā lābha santuṣṭaḥ dvandvātītaḥ vimatsaraḥ samaḥ siddhau asiddhau ca kṛtvā api na nibadhyate
yadṛcchā-lābha-santuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ | samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate ||22||
docs.text: Content with whatever comes of its own accord, free from the pairs of opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure — such a person, even while acting, is never bound by karma.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.22

tags: gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñāna avasthita cetasaḥ yajñāya ācarataḥ karma samagram pravilīyate
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-cetasaḥ | yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate ||23||
docs.text: For one who is free from attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who acts only as a sacrifice — all karma dissolves entirely.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.23

tags: brahma arpaṇam brahma haviḥ brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam brahma eva tena gantavyam brahma-karma-samādhinā
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samādhinā ||24||
docs.text: The act of offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman alone is to be reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.24

tags: daivam eva apare yajñam yoginaḥ paryupāsate brahmāgnau apare yajñena eva upajuhvati
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate | brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati ||25||
docs.text: Some yogis perform sacrifice by worshipping the gods alone; others offer the sacrifice itself as an oblation into the fire of Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.25

tags: śrotrādīni indriyāṇi anye saṁyama agniṣu juhvati śabdādīn viṣayān indriyāgniṣu
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṁyamāgniṣu juhvati | śabdādīn viṣayān anye indriyāgniṣu juhvati ||26||
docs.text: Some offer the senses such as hearing into the fires of self-restraint; others offer sense objects such as sound into the fires of the senses.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.26

tags: sarvāṇi indriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi ca apare ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi cāpare | ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite ||27||
docs.text: Others offer all the functions of the senses and the functions of the life-breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.27

tags: dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare | svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ ||28||
dravya-yajñāḥ tapo-yajñāḥ yoga-yajñāḥ tathā apare svādhyāya jñāna-yajñāḥ ca yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ
docs.text: Some offer their wealth as sacrifice, some offer austerity, some offer yoga, and others — ascetics of strict vows — offer self-study and knowledge as their sacrifice.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.28

tags: apāne juhvati prāṇam prāṇe apānam tathā apare prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe 'pānaṁ tathāpare | prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ ||29||
docs.text: Still others offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both — devoted to the practice of pranayama (breath control).
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.29

tags: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati sarve api ete yajña-vidaḥ yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati | sarve 'py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||30||
docs.text: Others, who regulate their diet, offer the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All of these are knowers of sacrifice, and their sins are destroyed through sacrifice.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.30

tags: yajña-śiṣṭa amṛta bhujaḥ yānti brahma sanātanam na ayam lokaḥ asti ayajñasya kutaḥ anyaḥ kuru-sattama
yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam | nāyaṁ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kuru-sattama ||31||
docs.text: Those who partake of the nectar of the remnants of sacrifice attain the eternal Brahman. Even this world is not for one who makes no sacrifice — how then any other world, O best of the Kurus?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.31

tags: evam bahu-vidhāḥ yajñāḥ vitatāḥ brahmaṇaḥ mukhe karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān jñātvā vimokṣyase
evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe | karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||32||
docs.text: Thus, many kinds of sacrifices are described in the Vedas. Know them all to be born of action. Knowing this, you shall be liberated.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.32

tags: śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa | sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||33||
śreyān dravya-mayāt yajñāt jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa sarvam karma akhilam pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
docs.text: The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to any material sacrifice, O scorcher of foes. All actions in their entirety, O Partha, culminate in knowledge.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.33

tags: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā | upadekṣyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ ||34||
tat viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā upadekṣyanti te jñānam jñāninaḥ tattva-darśinaḥ
docs.text: Learn that by prostrating yourself, by asking questions, and by rendering service. The wise ones, the seers of truth, will impart knowledge to you.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.34

tags: yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava | yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi ||35||
yat jñātvā na punaḥ moham yāsyasi pāṇḍava yena bhūtāni aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasi ātmani atho mayi
docs.text: Knowing which, you shall not again fall into delusion, O Pandava. By that knowledge, you shall see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.35

tags: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ | sarvaṁ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛjinaṁ santariṣyasi ||36||
api cet asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ sarvam jñāna-plavena eva vṛjinam santariṣyasi
docs.text: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.36

tags: yathaidhāṁsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna | jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||37||
yathā edhāṁsi samiddhaḥ agniḥ bhasmasāt kurute arjuna jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi tathā
docs.text: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all karma to ashes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.37

tags: na hi jñānena sadṛśam pavitram iha vidyate tat svayam yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālena ātmani vindati
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitram iha vidyate | tat svayaṁ yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati ||38||
docs.text: In this world, there is nothing as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga finds that knowledge spontaneously in the Self, in due course of time.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.38

tags: śraddhāvān labhate jñānam tat-paraḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇa adhigacchati
śraddhāvāṁl labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ | jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śāntim acireṇādhigacchati ||39||
docs.text: The faithful one, devoted to knowledge and having mastered the senses, attains knowledge. Having attained knowledge, one quickly reaches supreme peace.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.39

tags: ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṁśayātmā vinaśyati | nāyaṁ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṁ saṁśayātmanaḥ ||40||
ajñaḥ ca aśraddadhānaḥ saṁśayātmā vinaśyati na ayam lokaḥ paraḥ sukham saṁśayātmanaḥ
docs.text: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubter perish. For the doubting soul, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor any happiness.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.40

tags: yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇam jñāna-sañchinna-saṁśayam ātmavantam na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇaṁ jñāna-sañchinna-saṁśayam | ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||41||
docs.text: One who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubts have been destroyed by knowledge, and who is self-possessed — actions do not bind such a person, O Dhananjaya.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.41

tags: tasmād ajñāna-sambhūtaṁ hṛt-sthaṁ jñānāsinātmanaḥ | chittvainaṁ saṁśayaṁ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata ||42||
tasmāt ajñāna-sambhūtam hṛt-stham jñānāsinā ātmanaḥ chittvā enam saṁśayam yogam ātiṣṭha uttiṣṭha bhārata
docs.text: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder the doubt born of ignorance residing in your heart. Take refuge in yoga. Arise, O Bharata!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.42

tags: arjuna uvāca sannyāsam karmaṇām kṛṣṇa punaḥ yogam ca śaṁsasi yat śreyaḥ etayoḥ ekam tat me brūhi suniścitam
